text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark has every chance of becoming a leader in trading on the Internet. Today Denmark is one of the countries in the world where people are most familiar with new technology, a new survey shows.

--- More companies are demanding that prospective employees have no criminal records and the number of job applicants asking the police to prove that they have no records has tripled within only a few years.
--- Denmark became a net energy exporter in 1996 for the first time, contributing more than 500,000 million crowns to the trade balance, Energy Minister Svend Auken said.

--- US warships are allowed in Greenlandic waters with nuclear weapons today, new documents state, even though foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen maintains that the policy of no nuclear weapons on Danish territory has been respected since a US nuclear bomber crashed in Greenland in 1968.
--- Employment in the construction industry is expected to peak in 1997 following a slight fall in public building programmes.
--- Exports of windmills to Germany worth 500,000 million crowns could be hurt if German politicians adopt a law cutting the price that electricity suppliers pay for power from windmills.
